purpose.statement: Media helps people understand, create, restore, enhance, edit, animate, simulate, synchronize, compose, assess, and deliver governed audio, video, image, speech, spatial, and time-based work. Users can move from intent to reviewable output while retaining source material, seeing material changes, and understanding what is measured, estimated, reconstructed, generated, or unknown. Media does not claim the domain authority of a scientific, pedagogical, clinical, rights, or publication owner.
purpose.forWhom: Canonical actor records: media.creator, media.editor, media.reviewer, media.developer-integrator, media.automation-client, media.operator, media.administrator, media.privacy-rights-reviewer, media.worker, media.external-provider, media.domain-reviewer.

scope.description: The intended Media product scope spans understanding, creation, restoration, enhancement, editing, animation, simulation, synchronization, composition, mastering, quality assessment, and delivery of governed media. Inclusion in this scope defines product meaning; it does not assert that a capability is implemented, licensed, qualified, or available in any runtime.
inclusions: image, video, audio, and music creation
media-specific visual recognition and temporal/scene-text semantics
exclusions: generic Document Intelligence/OCR runtime and parser providers
generic model/provider router, credentials, quota, and failover
generic identity, workflow, audit, observability, and product-development frameworks
Data Cloud governed metadata/read-model and compatibility ownership
pedagogical truth, clinical decisions, campaign claims, and scientific model authority
external provider certification and legal/rights determinations
Explorer simulations as evidence of production runtime behavior

nonGoals.description: Media will not implement or own generic document OCR, extraction, parser or document-management engines.
nonGoals.reason: MDI-001 assigns their public contracts to Shared and runtime execution to Document Intelligence; Media owns temporal scene-text mappings only.

nonGoals.description: Media will not create competing identity, authorization, workflow, event, audit, observability, governance or generic AI routing frameworks.
nonGoals.reason: Public Ghatana Shared and platform contracts own these mechanics; Media supplies domain-specific intent and adapters.

nonGoals.description: Media will not own a competing product-definition, Explorer, evidence or Lifecycle closure framework.
nonGoals.reason: Ghatana Tools and Lifecycle own the public schemas, generic host mechanics, proof admission and receipts.

nonGoals.description: Media presentation and simulation will not claim independent clinical, pedagogical, scientific or rights adjudication.
nonGoals.reason: Specialized domain owners and verified external authorities retain the meaning and approval of such claims.

nonGoals.description: Media will not promise every codec, model, voice, hardware profile, provider or format to be universally licensed, qualified or available.
nonGoals.reason: Implementation, model or asset licensing, technical qualification and profile availability are independent admission dimensions.

actors.name: creator
actors.description: Turn an idea, brief, or source material into a governed media result. May initiate only actions authorized for the current identity and project; creation intent is not a license grant, privacy exception, or publication approval.
responsibilities: Express intent and review proposed inputs, constraints, and material tradeoffs.
Supply or select source material only within applicable rights and access policy.
Review and accept outputs where the workflow requires creator acceptance.

actors.name: editor
actors.description: Make controlled, reviewable changes while preserving source material and accepted revisions. Editing authority is limited to the selected project and authorized assets; an edit or local approval does not reverse a completed external publication.
responsibilities: Edit through versioned, non-destructive operations.
Review changed regions, timing, quality, and provenance before accepting a revision.

actors.name: reviewer
actors.description: Decide whether an exact version meets its stated review purpose. Review authority is purpose- and scope-limited. A review does not imply rights clearance, scientific validation, or publication permission unless separately assigned and authorized.
responsibilities: Review the version, context, evidence, and requested review criteria.
Record a decision that remains bound to that exact version and purpose.

actors.name: developer integrator
actors.description: Integrate Media through supported contracts and maintain compatible clients and workflows. Integration access is controlled by credentials and scopes; developer status does not authorize access to customer content or production effects.
responsibilities: Use documented public APIs, SDKs, CLI contracts, and integration boundaries.
Surface contract errors and finality without inventing product state.

actors.name: automation client
actors.description: Automate repeatable, declared media workflows with inspectable inputs and outcomes. Automation inherits only its scoped machine identity and delegated policy; it cannot infer a retry-safe outcome from timeout or lost observation.
responsibilities: Submit bounded requests through the public API/SDK/CLI contract.
Preserve idempotency, cancellation, and unknown-finality semantics.

actors.name: operator
actors.description: Maintain service operation and help resolve blocked or degraded work safely. Operational access does not grant content rights or permission to alter customer assets, bypass product policy, or claim a job outcome without evidence.
responsibilities: Inspect health, bounded diagnostics, queue/service state, and safe recovery options.
Preserve job, audit, and artifact finality while responding to incidents.

actors.name: administrator
actors.description: Configure approved product and tenant settings within assigned scope. Administrative status is scoped and policy-derived; it does not imply unrestricted access to media contents, rights, approval, or external publication.
responsibilities: Apply reviewed configuration and manage scoped identities/settings.
Keep configuration changes auditable and reversible where safe.

actors.name: privacy rights reviewer
actors.description: Assess whether a processing or lifecycle decision respects privacy, consent, retention, and rights obligations. Review conclusions are advisory or gating only as defined by an assigned policy/approval contract; review does not invent legal rights or waive policy.
responsibilities: Review relevant processing purpose, data flow, consent, rights, retention, and deletion implications.
Identify required approvals or unresolved policy conditions before a consequential effect.

actors.name: worker
actors.description: Execute the admitted processing step and preserve traceable, bounded results. A worker is not a user or approver. It must not widen its plan, silently downgrade quality or policy, or use generic document-intelligence internals.
responsibilities: Validate its scoped inputs and plan, enforce resource/cancellation bounds, and report outputs and failures.
Preserve provenance and avoid unauthorized side effects.

actors.name: external provider
actors.description: Complete only the provider operation requested under an admitted contract. A provider is not an authority for Media product semantics, rights, quality acceptance, approval, or final external effects.
responsibilities: Return contract-defined result, error, provenance, and execution identity where supported.
Honor the admitted data-processing and execution boundary.

actors.name: domain reviewer
actors.description: Review a declared domain model, unit system, assumptions, and fidelity boundary for a specific purpose. The role does not itself grant access or approval. A relevant domain owner must appoint the reviewer and define the evidence basis; no scientific, clinical, pedagogical, legal, or safety conclusion is implied without the applicable owner contract.
responsibilities: Identify the relevant domain authority and scope for a review.
Assess declared assumptions and evidence only within the assigned domain scope.
Record uncertainty, exclusions, and required owner follow-up.

businessIntents.description: Integrating products reuse public governed Media capabilities without creating incompatible per-product media execution authorities.
Reviewers and integrating products can distinguish originals, exact derived versions, uncertainty and authorized delivery.
Processing execution has declared supported profiles with controlled policy, budget, resource and failure behavior.
Long-running jobs remain observable and safely reconcilable without blind replay or misleading cancellation outcomes.

All input, decoding, import, model, scene, shader, script, and archive processing is bounded and isolated before content is promoted to trusted usable state.
Tenant, classification, consent, purpose, residency, egress, provider-retention, training, and rights remain independent policy axes at every applicable processing boundary.
Required external effects have durable accountable intent before dispatch; uncertain effects are never replayed merely to repair missing evidence.
Operational logs, traces, metrics, audit, and provenance have distinct schemas and retention; redaction failure never falls back to raw sensitive content.
Every supported task is keyboard operable with visible focus and non-drag alternatives; screen-reader output exposes selected media objects, measurements, status, and permitted actions.
UI locale, speech language, subtitle language, voice locale, and metadata/time formatting are independent; unsupported languages are declared unavailable rather than silently substituted.
The primary experience is intent-first with progressive disclosure; expert controls and provider details do not burden ordinary users or hide consequential choices.
Control-plane and local interaction performance is measured separately from external model, render, simulation, and encoding work on frozen reference environments.
Every job and optimization has finite CPU, memory, storage, GPU, process, time, retry, and monetary bounds; each fallback rechecks budget and quality authority.
Sample, frame, clip, and event timestamps use explicit rational clocks and declared rounding/resampling rules with no silent drift.
Scientific/domain fidelity is separate from visual quality; quality measures state applicability and abstention, and never override rights or domain constraints.
Restart, retry, cancellation, restore, and reconciliation preserve identity, idempotency, fences, erasure tombstones, and uncertainty.

Local-development, private-local, connected-production, and hybrid-production are explicit capability-scoped contracts; no profile silently enables network egress, model download, or a lower-fidelity fallback.
Production SLO, RPO, RTO, restore, and soak limits are owner-approved and backed by deployment-specific observation before activation.

domainRules.name: Machine-scoped state identity
domainRules.rule: A state identifier is meaningful only together with its machine; equal spellings across job, attempt, upload, stream, or delivery machines do not establish equivalent state or behavior.
domainRules.rationale: Preserve the owner-adjudicated machine-scoped identity rule and reject lossy cross-machine normalization.

domainRules.name: Request receipt is not queued execution
domainRules.rule: A request receipt or ACCEPTED response proves receipt only; it does not prove durable queueing, worker claim, dispatch, or execution.
domainRules.rationale: Keep ingress acknowledgment distinct from job state and attempt execution.

domainRules.name: Unknown outcome remains unresolved
domainRules.rule: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is neither running nor failure nor safe-to-retry; preserve uncertainty until an authoritative reconciliation resolves the effect.
domainRules.rationale: Prevent a lossy observation from authorizing duplicate external effects.

domainRules.name: Completion is distinct from delivery acknowledgment
domainRules.rule: A completed job requires the operation-defined output set, integrity, authority, and durable result commit; it does not establish recipient delivery acknowledgment.
domainRules.rationale: Keep result finality separate from external delivery evidence.

domainRules.name: Cancellation requires authoritative finality
domainRules.rule: A cancellation request or observer detachment does not establish cancellation; cancellation requires authoritative no-dispatch or confirmed fenced-effects finality under the operation contract.
domainRules.rationale: Keep request intent and observed cancellation result distinct.

domainRules.name: Partial success requires closed effect accounting
domainRules.rule: PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED is terminal only when every declared sub-effect has an explicit closed disposition and no consequential effect remains unknown.
domainRules.rationale: Prevent unresolved effects from being hidden by an aggregate partial-success label.

invariants.statement: A private context does not imply local processing, and local processing does not imply authorized use.

journeys.name: First use, authentication, context, and project creation
steps: Authenticate through the admitted identity contract and select an authorized tenant/workspace.
A versioned empty project exists and the creator sees a safe next action without selecting a provider/model/engine.

journeys.name: Upload/import, inspect, and produce a usable artifact
steps: Source selection and upload are authorized; current consent/retention rules are checked.
Original bytes remain identifiable and an artifact version has integrity and available technical metadata recorded.

journeys.name: Audio/video transcription through corrected captions
steps: Audio/video access, language intent, and required consent/processing policy are available.
Timestamped transcript/caption draft is reviewable with language, timing, provenance, uncertainty, and exact source version.

journeys.name: Authorized text-to-speech to approved audio
steps: Text, voice rights/consent, language and output intent are admitted.
A reviewable audio artifact records selected voice/version, format/rate, provenance, and approval status where required.

journeys.name: Image/video analysis, geometry, and tracks
steps: Source and analysis purpose are authorized; technical input limits are explicit.
Observations retain source artifact, timestamp/frame/region, model provenance, and confidence/uncertainty.

journeys.name: Multimodal or document consumer request to grounded typed result
steps: Consumer purpose and artifact access are authorized; Media-specific scene-text intent is distinguished from document extraction.
A typed result returns source/time/region/provenance and explicit uncertainty; generic document parsing remains with Document Intelligence.

journeys.name: Noisy/clipped interview cleanup with preservation and comparison
steps: Source and requested preservation profile are admitted.
A derived output and before/after comparison disclose processing and reconstruction limits.

journeys.name: Low-quality video repair with measured comparison
steps: Repair operation, input envelope, and budget are admitted by P0-003/P0-007.
Eligible stabilized/upscaled/repaired output is compared under applicable metrics with limitations visible.

journeys.name: Prompt/brief to storyboard, composition, render, review, and delivery
steps: Intent, source/reference rights, budget, quality/preservation choices, and required reviewers are explicit.
Exact output version is reviewed, approved as required, and delivered with an accurate external-effect status.

journeys.name: Controlled generation with references and continuity review
steps: Reference/control uses are rights-checked; protected identity and geometry constraints are explicit.
Candidate sequence is reviewed for continuity with uncertainty/provenance exposed.

journeys.name: Region mask/tracking edit with comparison and undo
steps: Edit is bound to an exact artifact version, frame/time range, and authorized operation.
Region edit is versioned and reviewable; source and prior edit remain recoverable.

journeys.name: Deterministic 2D/vector/procedural animation
steps: Animation controls and exact timing/export subset are declared.
Accessible preview and export preserve declared curve/time semantics.

journeys.name: 3D character, rig, path, or control animation
steps: Scene/rig assets, coordinate convention, rights, and supported interchange subset are identified.
Render/export binds animation to a declared rig/scene version and reports conversion loss.

journeys.name: Explore a domain simulation and its measurements
steps: Domain owner/model, equations, unit-bearing conditions, validity range, solver envelope, and fidelity tier are referenced.
Measurements/passes and any animation/render remain traceable to domain model and declared fidelity.

journeys.name: Simulation/procedural passes with protected semantic validation
steps: Domain truth and protected semantic properties are identified before any generative refinement.
Refinement preserves accepted domain measurements or reports the exact failed validation and fidelity consequence.

journeys.name: Existing-video translation/dubbing and voice/timing review
steps: Source, translation intent, voice authority, subtitle/voice locales, and destination are independently specified.
Mastered version is synchronized, reviewed for meaning and timing, and delivered only with required approval.

journeys.name: Music, effects, Foley, stems, mix, and mastering
steps: Source/license scope, target profile, channel layout, and mastering intent are explicit.
Mix/master output records profile, loudness/peak measurements where applicable, and source lineage.

journeys.name: Compose clips, captions, exact graphics, color, and audio master
steps: Exact assets/fonts/brand claims, timeline mapping, color profile, and output destination are authorized.
Versioned composition renders with deterministic exact graphics and declared audiovisual/color profile.

journeys.name: Review media quality and improve it within declared limits
steps: Applicable metrics, thresholds, budget, stop conditions, and protected properties are defined.
User selects or declines a measurable successor candidate with estimated/reconstructed properties disclosed.

journeys.name: Observe a long-running job and check its outcome safely
steps: Job has stable request/attempt identity and durable status contract.
User observes completion or known uncertainty; cancellation/retry/reconciliation preserves completed work.

journeys.name: Review/comment/approve exact version and re-review changed material
steps: Review purpose, exact artifact version, reviewer authority, and scope/expiry are explicit.
Decision attaches to the reviewed version and required approval state.

journeys.name: Export/download/publish with destination acknowledgement
steps: Exact output, destination, rights, approval, and external-effect authority are current.
Package validity, transport, and external publication are reported as distinct finality outcomes.

journeys.name: Private/local workflow while disconnected and reconnect
steps: An admitted local capability, offline mode, cached asset permission, and storage policy are explicitly established.
Only work allowed in the admitted disconnected mode is completed; reconnect reconciles versions and jobs without remote fallback.

journeys.name: CLI batch/JSON plan through verified outputs
steps: Public command/request schema, explicit approval/policy input, client keys, and per-item budgets are accepted.
Each item reports its terminal/partial/unknown outcome and output refs using the same semantics as other channels.

journeys.name: Agent or product integration with bounded delegated Media action
steps: Public Media action, bounded authority/delegation, recursion/cost limits, and return contract are admitted.
Caller receives an opaque job/result reference and truthful status; any consequential effect has separate authority.

journeys.name: Delete/revoke/retention/hold and visible lifecycle
steps: Identity, deletion/revocation authority, retention/hold state, and affected artifact/derivative scope are resolved.
Product lifecycle reflects completion/partial/blocked status without claiming remote copies were recalled.

journeys.name: Continue safely when processing is unavailable
steps: Capability qualification, license, runtime availability, and fallback policy are checked independently.
User receives an admitted equivalent fallback with material differences disclosed or a clear blocked result.

journeys.name: Spatial/360/interactive/synthetic-data export to declared consumer
steps: Destination subset, coordinate/time conventions, synthetic-data labeling, and licensing are declared.
Consumer receives an identified package and conversion report with unsupported/lossy features disclosed.

journeys.name: Live session loss, consent change, and bounded recovery
steps: A live session has stable session/frame identity, bounded buffers, a current lease, and authoritative consent scope.
The session is confirmed closed/drained or its in-flight external effects remain explicitly unknown; no new frame crosses the boundary after revocation or fencing.

journeys.name: Check which processing options are eligible
steps: Identity, tenant/workspace scope, and diagnostic permissions are verified; profile, capability, provider, license, qualification, and runtime dimensions are represented separately.
The caller receives a bounded, current observation with provenance and explicit unknown/unsupported dimensions; an observation does not promise future availability.

businessIntentMeasureProposals.description: Eligible consumer workflows using versioned public contracts and preserved domain finality.

contract.description: Eligible consumer workflows using versioned public contracts and preserved domain finality.
contract.populationEnumeration: Source applicability is enumerated per exact leaf; named admitted consumer/profile cohort and qualified observations remain NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.profileBinding: Freeze the release-profile ID and contract versions, selected exact capability leaves, deployment/region, tenant-policy scope, observation interval, and consumer cohort before counting. A fixture, candidate profile, or unversioned integration is not an admitted workflow.
contract.numerator: Count denominator workflows with a current public contract version and passing consumer conformance for every bound operation, including preserved idempotency, cancellation, status, and finality distinctions.
contract.denominator: Count distinct consumer workflows declared in the frozen release-profile cohort that invoke at least one bound public Media capability; retain failed, blocked, and untested workflows in the denominator. Exclude a workflow only when it is outside the declared cohort or no bound public capability applies, and record that reason.
contract.calculation: 100 * numerator / denominator; report percent and raw numerator/denominator integers. A zero denominator is NOT_APPLICABLE, never 100 percent; incomplete inventory or evidence is NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.valueUnit: percent; retain raw integer numerator and denominator with each observation.
contract.baselinePolicy: Establish only from a complete frozen cohort and observation interval using the same conformance oracle for every workflow; include failures and abstentions, preserve versioned evidence, and do not extrapolate from fixtures or request volume.
contract.targetPolicy: NOT_SET until Media owners select an explicit release-profile threshold after a qualified baseline and calibration review; do not assume 100 percent or transfer a target between profiles.
contract.applicability: Only workflows admitted for the named release profile and public contract version; internal fixtures alone do not count as admitted consumers.
contract.acceptanceCriterion: Every counted workflow identifies its contract version and has evidence that the consumer preserves the bound Media operation's finality distinctions.
contract.ownerRecommendation: Measure adoption as a distinct consumer-workflow conformance ratio, not call volume; repeated requests do not create additional workflows and a workflow with any failing bound operation does not enter the numerator.
contract.baseline: NOT_EVALUATED; no admitted consumer inventory is recorded by this product definition.
contract.target: NOT_SET; set only after a named release profile and qualified baseline are selected.

businessIntentMeasureProposals.description: Applicable output contracts specifying exact identity, provenance, rights state and delivery acknowledgment.

contract.description: Applicable output contracts specifying exact identity, provenance, rights state and delivery acknowledgment.
contract.populationEnumeration: The exact 430-leaf candidate source set is enumerated per leaf in ownerCapabilityApplicabilityCrosswalk by owner outcome and declared outputArtifactTypes. Candidate scope includes incomplete, missing, or rejected output contracts; admitted profiles plus qualified observations remain NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.profileBinding: Freeze the named release-profile ID, exact output-producing capability operation contract versions, delivery profile, preservation mode, jurisdiction/ policy scope, and observation interval. Evaluate each applicable capability/profile pair once.
contract.numerator: Count applicable output-operation-contract/profile pairs whose versioned contract defines immutable output identity and lineage, current rights state separately from user attestation, and completion separately from recipient acknowledgment.
contract.denominator: Count every output-producing operation-contract/profile pair selected in the frozen release profile, including pairs with missing, rejected, or incomplete contracts. Exclude read-only operations only with a source-linked non-output rationale recorded per pair.
contract.calculation: 100 * numerator / denominator; report percent and raw numerator/denominator integers. A zero denominator is NOT_APPLICABLE, never complete; an unenumerated applicable output population is NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.valueUnit: percent; retain raw integer numerator and denominator with each observation.
contract.baselinePolicy: Establish only from a complete frozen output-capability/profile inventory and versioned contract audit; retain failed, missing, blocked, and unassessed pairs, and do not infer current coverage from generated artifacts.
contract.targetPolicy: NOT_SET until owners choose a profile-specific threshold after qualified baseline review; do not treat all contracts as a target or waive identity, rights, provenance, or acknowledgment criteria to meet one.
contract.applicability: An output is counted only when its operation can produce or deliver an output under the named profile; read-only and non-output operations are outside the denominator with an explicit rationale.
contract.acceptanceCriterion: Each counted contract defines immutable output identity and lineage, represents rights state separately from user attestation, and distinguishes result completion from recipient acknowledgment.
contract.ownerRecommendation: Use the operation-contract/profile pair as the stable unit; one operation exposed in two delivery profiles is two units, while multiple output artifacts from one invocation are not extra units. Capability references are source traces only and do not substitute for the not-yet-enumerated operation population.
contract.baseline: NOT_EVALUATED; applicable operations and runtime evidence have not been qualified as a complete population.
contract.target: NOT_SET; no numeric target is asserted before profile applicability and a qualified baseline are established.

businessIntentMeasureProposals.description: Admitted execution profiles with qualified bounds and classified unsupported cases.

contract.description: Admitted execution profiles with qualified bounds and classified unsupported cases.
contract.populationEnumeration: Exact 394 execution-profile candidates are enumerated per leaf by output role, operation, profile, and bounds; local and external execution are both included, and selected environments and qualification remain NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.profileBinding: Freeze the exact Media execution-profile ID/version, capability leaf, provider/model/codec versions, deployment/hardware, region, policy and rights scope, input envelope, and observation interval. Profile axes are independent dimensions; no axis value implies another.
contract.numerator: Count selected capability/profile pairs with an admitted dependency set, explicit input/resource/policy/failure bounds, and qualified observations covering each claimed bound and declared unsupported case.
contract.denominator: Count every execution capability/profile pair declared in the frozen release profile, including unavailable, unsupported, unqualified, and failed pairs. Exclude a pair only when it is explicitly outside the frozen profile and retain the disposition.
contract.calculation: 100 * numerator / denominator; report percent and raw numerator/denominator integers. A zero denominator is NOT_APPLICABLE, never full coverage; absent capability inventory or qualification evidence is NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.valueUnit: percent; retain raw integer numerator and denominator with each observation.
contract.baselinePolicy: Establish only with the exact pinned capability/dependency/environment and input envelope; include unsupported and failed selected pairs, and retain separate qualification records for each claimed bound.
contract.targetPolicy: NOT_SET until the owner selects profile-specific bound coverage after qualified observations; no throughput, latency, quality, or availability threshold is inferred here.
contract.applicability: A profile is counted only after its provider, model or codec dependencies and exact execution environment are selected; unselected profiles are not implicitly supported.
contract.acceptanceCriterion: Each counted profile has explicit input and resource bounds, rights and policy preconditions, failure/finality behavior, and source-backed unsupported cases, with qualification evidence for every claimed runtime bound.
contract.ownerRecommendation: Count exact capability/profile combinations, not provider names or profile labels; a claimed resource or latency bound requires a measurement under the same pinned environment and input envelope.
contract.baseline: NOT_EVALUATED; no complete set of admitted execution profiles is recorded.
contract.target: NOT_SET; profile selection and qualified observations are prerequisites to a numeric target.

businessIntentMeasureProposals.description: Applicable job operations with stable identity, idempotency/fencing, recovery and unknown-finality proof.

contract.description: Applicable job operations with stable identity, idempotency/fencing, recovery and unknown-finality proof.
contract.populationEnumeration: Exact 445 asynchronous or timeout-ambiguous persisted operation candidates are enumerated per leaf; unknown completion behavior, including versioned recipe commands that may commit after interruption, stays in scope. The selected/admitted runtime population and qualified measurements remain NOT_EVALUATED. Exclusions require an exact synchronous non-job or non-dispatch source rationale.
contract.profileBinding: Freeze the release-profile ID, exact asynchronous job capability leaves and versions, persistence/deployment scope, retry and effect policy, and observation interval. Operation identity is the logical job capability/version, not an HTTP route or SDK method alias.
contract.applicabilityRule: Include one population unit only when the exact operation contract states that its submitted work can outlive the initiating request or returns a stable job reference for asynchronous execution. Status, watch, cancel, and retry commands are evidence inputs for that submission's recovery contract; they are not separate long-running-operation units by name alone. Record a per-operation inclusion or exclusion rationale.
contract.numerator: Count denominator asynchronous operation/profile pairs whose contracts and executable evidence establish stable logical and attempt identity, idempotent/fenced retry behavior, cancellation finality, recoverable state, and authoritative unknown-outcome reconciliation.
contract.denominator: Count every asynchronous operation-contract/profile pair exposed by the frozen release profile, including operations with missing or failed recovery evidence. A synchronous operation is excluded only after the exact source contract establishes it cannot outlive the initiating request.
contract.calculation: 100 * numerator / denominator; report percent and raw numerator/denominator integers. A zero denominator is NOT_APPLICABLE, never fully recoverable; incomplete operation inventory or missing proof is NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.valueUnit: percent; retain raw integer numerator and denominator with each observation.
contract.baselinePolicy: Establish only from the complete asynchronous operation inventory for the frozen release profile and versioned reconciliation evidence; include failed or unproved operations and preserve unknown outcomes as unresolved.
contract.targetPolicy: NOT_SET until owners select a profile-specific recovery threshold after qualified failure-injection and reconciliation observations; a request or cancellation acknowledgment is not terminal completion evidence.
contract.applicability: Include only operations that can outlive the initiating request; synchronous read-only queries and operations excluded by the selected profile are not counted.
contract.acceptanceCriterion: Each counted operation defines stable job and attempt identity, duplicate/retry behavior, stale-worker fencing, cancellation finality, recovery actions, and an authoritative unknown-outcome reconciliation path.
contract.ownerRecommendation: Treat unknown outcomes and cancellation requests as unresolved until authoritative reconciliation; do not count retries or user-visible status labels as proof of recovery. Derive the denominator from per-operation asynchronous submission semantics, not command-family membership or similarly named transport methods.
contract.baseline: NOT_EVALUATED; current proposals do not constitute runtime proof.
contract.target: NOT_SET; establish after the applicable operation set and qualified runtime profile are selected.
